postTitle: Refinancing: When to Refinance and When to Wait
topic: Should you refinance? Only if you keep the loan past its break even month

assumptions.notes: Blog example: closing costs €4,000, monthly saving €200, break even 4,000 / 200 = month 20. Held 60 months: (60 - 20) x 200 = €8,000 ahead; held 24 months: €800. Ignores rate, tax and term changes and the opportunity cost of the costs. Common guideline from the blog: hold period often 2x the break even or more.

beats.narration: A refinance has costs up front: say four thousand euros.
Then it saves you two hundred a month.
Twenty months of savings pay those costs back.
So it depends how long you keep the loan. Sell before month twenty and it comes out behind.

If a refinance saves you €200 a month, when has it actually paid off?

Should you refinance? Here, €4,000 of costs and €200 a month saved break even at month 20. Keep the loan longer and it comes out ahead; sell sooner and it comes out behind. Many people look for keeping it about twice that long. Part 2: it passes the check, but should you wait for a lower rate?
